capabilities: encrypt Markdown notes in memory with a single password
authenticate and encrypt contents using AES256-GCM
restrict encryption to files with the .aes256 extension
extras: The README warns of possible data loss on unexpected errors and recommends periodic backups. Encryption only works in editing view, so the README instructs users to set editing view as the default for new tabs.
problem: Obsidian stores notes as plain local Markdown files with no built-in way to encrypt their contents at rest.
summary: Password-based, in-memory AES256-GCM encryption for Markdown notes saved with an .aes256 extension.
